title: Staying behind in New York when the cooperative band went home
summary: Cootie and Edmond Hall refused to go back to Florida, and lived on dime rolls and coffee from a Brooklyn baker.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yeah. So after the two weeks they were ready to go back. I said, "Not me." I said, "This is the place I've wanted to be all my life. I'm not thinking about going back to no Florida." And Helen, we was -- I was with the biggest band in the State of Florida. Colored band. And during that time, it was a cooperative band, making $150.00 a week during them times.
When Chick was at the Savoy, they were making $35.00 a week.
In other words, you were splitting the profits.
And I didn't have nothing to go to here. But I didn't go back with them. Me and Edmond Hall stayed.
Did you have any cash in your pocket?
Yeah. I had a little cash. I used to send my father all my money.
My father had lost all my money, his money, everybody's money.

So I wrote home for some money and my father sent me $50.00. And after all that was gone, I wrote home for some more money. My father told me he didn't have no more money. And I found a place in Brooklyn. Me and Edmond Hall found a place in Brooklyn where there was a baker's shop,
where we used to get our breakfast for a dime. And you used to get rolls and coffee for a dime.
No. We used to eat in there.
We used to eat in there. We used to get rolls and coffee for a dime.
And for our lunch we used to get soup and bread for 15 cents. And that's what we ate for a long time.
